Sales Power Mapping

Turns "I'm meeting with this district" into paper you can actually work from in the room.
SKILL · CALL IT BY NAME

What it does

A contact list tells you who works there. A power map tells you who can move a decision. This skill researches a district or a whole user group from published sources, ranks by buying signal rather than size, sweeps the state law that changes what you are allowed to claim, and builds it into a briefing designed for someone standing up holding paper with a person waiting on them.

Two modes

ModeSayYou get
One district"Prep me for [district]" / "I'm meeting with [district]"Three tabs: the verdict and landmines, the named seats with who decides and who only blocks, then state law and what changed there recently.
A user group or event"There's a Skyward user group in [state]"Four tabs: everything true of the whole room stated once, an alphabetical badge-to-page index, one page per district, and a law page organised as "if they say X, you say Y."

Inside a Project you have to name it. Skills do not start on their own in a Claude.ai Project. Say "use sales power mapping" or describe the outcome and the Project will call it.

Why the district pages look the way they do

Every district gets its own page, alphabetical, with the same eight fields in the same position every time. That is deliberate: you find a page by the district on someone's badge in about five seconds, then read by position instead of hunting. Every page carries a verbatim opening line you can say out loud, built on a published fact about that district.

An earlier version organised the same research by department. It was rebuilt from scratch, because a briefing that scatters one district across four sections cannot be used in front of a customer.

The blanks are on purpose

Four fields on every district page ship empty and marked for you to fill: the Skyward platform, what they already run of ours, any live thread, and anything you must not say. Those live in Salesforce and in your own head. The skill has no access to either, and it will not guess.

This rule exists because it was broken once. A draft carried a relationship column inferred from a source that does not carry that traffic. It was wrong, and it was printed as fact in a document a seller would have carried into a meeting. A guess on a page in front of a customer is worse than a blank.

What you should bring

For a user group, a Salesforce view filtered to State = XX, Type = Customer, SIS = Skyward, pasted in. Public sources will not give you a state's Skyward customer list. If you do not have one, the skill falls back to the user group's own published steering committee and says on the front page that it is a working set rather than the full account list.

Good to know

It will not tell you a claim is safe when it is not. Anything it could not verify is marked as unverified in place, next to the claim, so you know which lines you can repeat to a district and which need a phone call first. "Not found" is a correct answer and it will say so rather than fill the gap.

Requirements

What this skill needs in order to run.

Skills - sta-html-report for the finished file.

Connectors / MCP servers - None, by design. It uses the public internet plus whatever you give it in the chat.

From you - the four fields above, and a district list for event mode.

If something is missing - a missing district list is LOUD and it will tell you. The SILENT one is the four blank fields: the briefing still builds and still looks finished, and the blanks are only obvious if you read the front page that lists them.
